A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDR-Bench research. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, module ablations, failure analyses and checker-reliability measurements, including Tables 2–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds agent-framework comparisons in Appendix B, Table A1.

M1.justification: The DDR task, minimal ReAct scaffold, SQL/Python interaction, insight generation and checklist evaluation remain unchanged. The additional frameworks are experimental comparators, not revisions to the proposed benchmark procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC, GLOBEM and 10-K with the same 291 task entities and 2,058 checklist items. Appendix B uses these existing datasets without introducing new task requirements or populations.

E2.justification: Table A1 adds comparisons labelled Plan-and-Execute, CoALA memory and AutoGen multi-agent against ReAct for three existing models. This is a focused extension of the comparisons; the original model roster and module comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added framework ablations use Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-30B-A3B and GPT-5-mini, extending the model configurations studied beyond the Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B module experiments in v1. Existing sampling, scoring procedures and experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a focused test of whether planning, memory and multi-agent scaffolding improve insight discovery across three models and three domains. It extends the existing module analysis; earlier reasoning, memory, proactive/reactive and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five checker-evaluation repetitions on approximately 10% of the data, the same variability measures in Table 7, and the same correlation tests. Table A1 adds point estimates without new run counts, seeds or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table A1 adds 27 framework-condition scores; its nine ReAct scores reproduce Table 2's item-averaged message-wise results. Memory and multi-agent scores are lower in every new comparison, while planning improves two 10-K cases, including GPT-5-mini from the ReAct reference of 46.35 to 49.82. Previously reported results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The DDR formulation, normalized exploration entropy in Equation 1, and termination-probability expression are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical results or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about investigatory intelligence, DDR-Bench and the limitations of scaling and external scaffolding. Appendix B supplies additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B extends the scaffold interpretation, suggesting that complex frameworks affect model confidence and induce premature termination or over-/under-thinking. It also qualifies the generally negative results with planning benefits in some settings. Existing interpretations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: The new acknowledgments identify use of KCL's CREATE computing environment, providing a limited resource disclosure. Existing prompts, processing descriptions and code/data access statements are unchanged; the new framework experiments do not supply detailed implementation settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Qiao et al. (2025) and Qiu et al. (2026) to related work, plus Sumers et al. (2023), Wang et al. (2023) and Wu et al. (2024) for the framework comparisons. The overall positioning relative to prior research is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Agent Framework Ablations appendix and acknowledgments, updates appendix letters and cross-references, and corrects 'Reseacher' to 'Researcher' in Figure 2. The main narrative and existing appendix prose are otherwise substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table A1 and makes a small text correction within Figure 2. Appendix text and some figures shift position as material reflows, but existing plots, table structures and visual encodings are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B and Table A1 broaden the evidence behind the existing scaffold conclusions beyond v1's single-model module experiments, including useful exceptions where planning helps. The gain is limited because the new comparisons lack detailed framework settings and uncertainty estimates, while the benchmark and principal findings remain unchanged.
